title: Small-bundle endpoint composition PRD, acceptance criteria and launch checklist
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Purpose: Ship a compact, opinionated bundle of four hosted inference endpoints (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank) optimized for developer-first adoption and predictable billing. This PRD defines minimal behaviors, required telemetry, rollout constraints, and an operator-friendly launch checklist. Audience: SDK users, Platform engineers, Support, Sales. Goals: 1) Provide a coherent surface across the four endpoints with consistent authentication, error semantics, and rate limit behavior. 2) Ensure latency and cost SLOs for the small-bundle tier (P95 latency targets and unit economics guidance). 3) Include automated acceptance gates (smoke, regression evals, telemetry thresholds) to prevent regressions at launch. Out of scope: multi-model routing, dedicated capacity, VPC/private installs for initial launch. Constraints: must be compatible with current SDKs, use existing runtime kernels, and not require infra changes beyond a single routing flag.
user_stories: As a developer, I can call a single lightweight endpoint bundle with a clear parameter to choose chat vs completions vs embeddings vs rerank so I can prototype quickly without juggling multiple APIs.
As an ML engineer, I can view per-route latency and token-cost dashboards for the bundle in Console to diagnose regressions.
As a PM, I can stage rollout to 5% traffic and automatically roll back if service-level telemetry crosses thresholds.
requirements: Functional: Expose four logical routes in the hosted endpoint: /v1/bundle/chat, /v1/bundle/completions, /v1/bundle/embeddings, /v1/bundle/rerank with shared auth and consistent response envelope.
Functional: Streaming for chat and completions should be supported using existing SSE protocol used by hosted API.
Functional: Embeddings must return deterministic float32 vectors of fixed dimension per model specification; include checksum in response metadata.
Functional: Rerank must accept candidate arrays up to 200 items, return stable ranking with score normalization and optional explain token highlighting.
Non-functional: P95 latency targets for the small-bundle tier: chat 1200ms (first byte), completions 800ms, embeddings 250ms, rerank 600ms for typical payloads as defined in perf matrix.
Non-functional: Request rate limiting should be consistent across routes; shared quota behavior must be documented in Console and SDKs.
Operational: Each route must emit token counts, model_id, variant, latency histograms, error codes, and cache-hit flags to the hosted telemetry pipeline.
Compatibility: Backwards compatibility with existing chat/completions SDK call shapes; SDK adapters will map legacy calls to bundle routes.
Security: All traffic must pass through existing API gateway and observability hooks; no new public ports.
acceptance_criteria: 1) API surface: Bundle routes accept documented payloads and return responses conforming to schema tests in api-contract-tests repo (green).
2) Telemetry: Console shows per-route P95 latency, error rate <0.5% for synthetic traffic, and per-token cost estimates in cost dashboards.
3) Performance: Synthetic perf harness shows P95 targets met on the hosted small-bundle capacity profile for three consecutive days under steady load.

4) Regression evals: A representative prompt set (1000 items) for chat/completions/embeddings/rerank must pass quality thresholds (no regressions vs baseline within tolerance) as recorded in eval-dashboard.
5) SDK: JS and Python SDK adapters available with integration tests passing that demonstrate authentication, retries, and streaming behavior.
6) Docs: Public Quickstart, parameter reference, and billing guidance published to docs site; post contains examples for migration from legacy endpoints.
7) Rollout tooling: Canary policy configured (5% initial, 50% after green) with automated rollback trigger based on error and latency thresholds defined in rollout policy doc.
8) Security/compliance: Security review completed and signoff recorded for hosted-2025.03 release; no open high-severity findings.
9) Support readiness: Playbook and runbook created and validated in runbook rehearsal with on-call rotation confirmed.
scope_changes: Initial scope included multi-model routing; removed to reduce launch risk — will be addressed in a follow-up epic (PM-770000).
Added streaming support for completions during scoping after SDK feedback on developer ergonomics (change approved 2025-02-14).
Reduced rerank max candidates from 500 to 200 to keep P95 latency within targets for small-bundle capacity profile.
Deferred embedding-checksum header to post-launch patch due to runtime dependency on serialization library (tracked as ENG-94012).
launch_checklist: Pre-launch: Finalize API contract and merge api-contract-tests (PR #GH-5123).
Pre-launch: SDK adapters merged and published (JS v1.12.0, Python v0.34.1).
Pre-launch: Perf harness stable for 72 hours under 95th pct synthetic load; screenshots archived in perf-run-2025-02-18.
Pre-launch: Docs published and reviewed by documentation owner; quickstart validated by sample app in repo sample-apps/bundle-demo.
Pre-launch: Security review completed — checklist items A-C closed and acceptance note uploaded to compliance-drive link.
Launch day: Enable canary at 5% traffic using rollout job "start-canary-bundle" and monitor first 30 minutes for error spikes.
Launch day: Support engineers on rotation, Slack incident channel created and pinned runbook link.
Post-launch: Increase canary to 50% after 24h green signals; full rollout after 72h green or manual approval.
Post-launch: Collect and review telemetry for cost-per-token and anomaly detection rules — adjust default batching hints if cost deviates >10% vs forecast.
Post-launch: Execute rollback scenario during first week in staging; verify rollback cut traffic to legacy endpoints and confirm stability.
notes: Trade-offs: Prioritized developer ergonomics and coherent surface for faster PLG adoption vs delaying advanced routing and dedicated capacity features.
Rollback plan: Toggle routing flag to legacy endpoints and pause inbound bundle tokens in API gateway; validate end-to-end in staging before unmute.
Monitoring signals: Key metrics: per-route P95 latency, 5-min error rate, token cost delta, model-variance rate. Alert thresholds documented in alerting-runbook.
Open question: Should rerank expose an explainable tokens field by default? Default set to opt-in to reduce payload size; revisit after 1.0 launch.
